text: Plaintiff's counsel used ChatGPT to draft portions of a fee-response brief and other filings, producing a false direct quotation attributed to a Ninth Circuit case (Osazuwa) and additional fabricated quotations across three further briefs, plus an inaccurate AI-generated case summary of a Third Circuit case (Ansell v. Green Acres). This was the terminal order in a three-stage sanctions proceeding that began with a July 8, 2026 order to show cause and a July 28, 2026 order finding the errors attributable to generative-AI misuse.
asserted_by: asserting party not identified in the indexed source fields
deployer: Elizabeth Tate, counsel for plaintiff Michael L. Ruiz
canonical_source_conflicted: Multiple AI-generated false quotations and an inaccurate case summary across four separate briefs, cited to non-existent supporting language in real Ninth and Third Circuit opinions
mitigation_gap: Counsel did not verify AI-generated quotations against the actual case text before filing, across multiple briefs and after at least one earlier warning within the same proceeding.
reliance_or_harm: The court issued a formal public reprimand of counsel, which she must report in any future context requiring disclosure of past attorney discipline. The court cited prior discipline, a pattern of misconduct, and counsel's substantial experience as aggravating factors. No monetary sanction, CLE requirement, or State Bar referral was ordered in this final order.
source_locator: Michael L. Ruiz v. Magellan Financial & Insurance Services, No. CV-23-02090-PHX-DWL (D. Ariz.), Doc. 179
